*thinking through this year's plan...*

I'm 55, been farming 30 years. My old man's about the same age, and it's just the two of us at home — the kids are grown and working in the city now. Twenty mu isn't huge but it isn't small either, and with just two pairs of hands you've got to be careful about what you take on.

**How I've split the land**

I've been doing the same thing for years: 8 mu of cabbage, three rounds in a year — spring, summer, autumn — and the other 12 mu is wheat-maize, same as just about everyone around here. I wouldn't change it. Cabbage pays better per mu but it's exhausting and you have to hire help at harvest. More than 8 mu and we'd drown in it. The wheat-maize land mostly runs itself with the contractors and the combine.

**The cabbage (8 mu)**

Spring crop — I start the seedlings in the little plastic shelter in February, transplant out late Feb. Summer crop goes in right after the spring one comes out, early June. Autumn crop late August, harvest runs into November.

For each round, I put down about two bags of compound fertilizer per mu before transplanting, then half a bag of urea after they take root, and another shot at heading. I've tried putting less — must've been six, seven years back — and the heads came up small and loose. Buyers don't want that, so I went back to my usual. Cabbage drinks water, I pump from the well every 10, 15 days if no rain. Electric pumping's not cheap but thirsty cabbage won't head.

And I have to spray — there's always some worm or rot. I ask the shop in town what everyone's buying this year and get the same. I hire about 15 days of help at each harvest — can't do the lifting and packing ourselves anymore.

**The wheat (12 mu)**

Plant mid-October after the autumn cabbage is cleared. One bag of compound per mu as base, then a bag of urea topdress when it's jointing in the spring. Three waterings — before winter to settle it, spring green-up, and once when the grain's filling. Usually gets me about 450 kg/mu. Little better in a good year, little worse if spring is dry.

**The maize (12 mu)**

Goes in right after wheat harvest — we race the calendar, can't waste a day. I hire the no-till planter guy who comes through the village. Compound at planting, urea when it's at big flare. Rain usually handles the water, maybe one pump in August if July was dry. I get about 500 kg/mu most years.

**Cash and labor worries**

Spring is tight for money — I have to buy seed and fertilizer before any cabbage money has come in. We live off what we put aside from last autumn's cabbage sale. If prices were bad last year, this year is harder. Labor is the bigger worry honestly — two people can't do three rounds of cabbage plus the wheat-maize alone. The contractors handle the grain, and I hire day-labor at cabbage harvest. If I couldn't get help, I'd cut back the cabbage to 5 or 6 mu.
